# Copilot / AI Agent Instructions for PolygonMigration

This file gives targeted, actionable guidance so an AI coding assistant can be immediately productive in this Django codebase.

Summary
- Purpose: Help migrate problems and testcases from Polygon to a local DB and Azure Blob Storage.
- Stack: Django 5.x, PostgreSQL, Azure Blob Storage SDK, Redis (optional), requests, g++ used for compiling custom checkers.

Quick start commands
- Create venv (Unix): `python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate`
- Install deps (note filename): `pip install -r requirement.txt`
- Run migrations: `python manage.py migrate`
- Create superuser: `python manage.py createsuperuser`
- Run dev server: `python manage.py runserver`
- Run tests: `python manage.py test`
- Collect static (production): `python manage.py collectstatic`

Where to look (high value files)
- `PolygonMigration/PolygonMigration/settings.py` — environment variables, required secrets (POLYGON_API_KEY, POLYGON_API_SECRET) and logging setup. Note: startup will raise if Polygon keys are missing.
- `PolygonMigration/manage.py` — standard Django entrypoint.
- `problems/polygon_api.py` — core Polygon integration and Azure/Redis interactions. Key responsibilities:
  - API signature generation (`_generate_api_sig`) and HTTP calls (`_make_request`).
  - Downloading/extracting problem packages (`download_and_extract_package`).
  - Fetching tests and storing/reading them from Redis using the app-specific prefix `polygon_migration_test_cases_{polygon_id}`.
  - Compiling custom checkers (`compile_custom_checker`) and uploading to Azure via `problems/AzureTestcase.AzureBlobManager`.
- `problems/AzureTestcase.py` — see here for Azure Blob upload helpers (imported dynamically by `polygon_api.py`).
- `users/` — custom `User` model and `users/backends.py` (email-based authentication). Settings use `AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'users.User'`.
- `problems/templates/`, `users/templates/` — app-level templates follow `app/templates/<app>/` convention.

Project-specific conventions & gotchas
- Requirements file is named `requirement.txt` (singular). Install scripts and CI must use that filename.
- `.env` location: `PolygonMigration/PolygonMigration/.env` (loaded via python-dotenv). Many runtime values depend on this `.env`.
- `settings.py` will throw if `POLYGON_API_KEY`/`POLYGON_API_SECRET` are not set. For local tests, provide dummy values in `.env`.
- Redis key prefix used by code: `polygon_migration_test_cases_{polygon_id}` — use this when inspecting cache or writing tests that assert Redis contents.
- Custom checker flow:
  - `polygon_api.fetch_custom_checker_file(...)` tries multiple `type` values (`source`, `resource`) and `.cpp` fallback.
  - `compile_custom_checker(...)` uses `g++` on PATH and respects `CUSTOM_CHECKER_DIR` env var.
  - If compilation fails, code uploads the source file as `.cpp` to Azure as a fallback.
- Azure integration: `upload_*` functions expect an `AzureBlobManager` class in `problems/AzureTestcase.py`. Credentials come from environment variables documented in `README.md`.

Editing & extension guidance for AI
- Prefer minimal, focused edits. Many functions in `polygon_api.py` are long — refactor into smaller helpers only with tests.
- When changing behavior that touches external services (Polygon, Redis, Azure):
  - Add a small integration-style test that stubs network calls (use `responses` or `requests-mock`).
  - For Azure/Redis, provide environment-driven toggles so unit tests can run offline.
- Do not remove the explicit check that requires `POLYGON_API_KEY`/`POLYGON_API_SECRET` unless also adding a safe fallback for tests.

Examples of useful quick tasks for an AI
- Add a unit test that verifies `_generate_api_sig` returns the expected `apiSig` format (mock `time` and `random`).
- Add a safe wrapper around `requests.post` to centralize retries and timeouts, then replace direct calls in `polygon_api.py`.
- Create a management command `python manage.py migrate_polygon <id>` that uses `PolygonAPI` to fetch and save a problem — this makes manual testing easier.

Runtime & debugging tips
- If `manage.py runserver` fails immediately with an exception about Polygon keys, set dummy values in `.env` to let the server start.
- Logs: `logs/project.log` (file handler configured in `settings.py`) and console logger for `problems` is at DEBUG level by default. Use these while debugging uploads/fetches.
- When testing custom checker compilation locally, ensure `g++` is installed and `CUSTOM_CHECKER_DIR` is writable.

Where to update this file
- Merge content when `.github/copilot-instructions.md` already exists in future — prefer preserving repository-specific calls and not replacing with generic templates.
